speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the location and character of your headache, and have you noticed any specific visual changes like blurriness or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience pain or tenderness when chewing food or touching your scalp, and have you noticed any jaw pain or color changes in your vision like halos or temporary blindness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any scalp tenderness or jaw claudication, and have you noticed any changes in your vision color or transient visual obscurations? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age and symptoms, I need to rule out vascular causes despite the normal inflammatory markers. Have you noticed any new neurological deficits such as weakness, numbness, or speech difficulties, and does the headache worsen with changes in posture or exertion? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_with_contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain_with_contrast: No acute infarction, mass, or hemorrhage identified. Mild nonspecific white matter hyperintensities consistent with age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI ruled out structural causes and inflammatory markers are normal, I need to look at the eyes directly. Have you experienced any recent eye pain, redness, or sensitivity to light, and do you have a history of glaucoma or hypertension? REQUEST TEST: Ophthalmology_Exam

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Visual Acuity: Right Eye 20/120, Left Eye 20/80; Fundoscopy: Findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the fundoscopic findings of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages, I suspect an underlying vascular or hypercoagulable issue. Do you have a history of diabetes, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol, and have you noticed any swelling or pain in your legs? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Profile, Fasting_Glucose, Lipid_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Coagulation_Profile: PT 12.5 sec, INR 1.0, aPTT 30 sec (Normal); Fasting_Glucose: 95 mg/dL (Normal); Lipid_Panel: Total Cholesterol 190 mg/dL, LDL 110 mg/dL, HDL 55 mg/dL, Triglycerides 130 mg/dL (Normal)

speaker: Doctor
text: Since standard vascular risk factors and coagulation studies are normal, I need to investigate potential hypercoagulable states or local orbital issues. Do you have a history of smoking, hormone replacement therapy, or autoimmune conditions like antiphospholipid syndrome? REQUEST TEST: Antiphospholipid_Antibodies, Orbital_CT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Antiphospholipid_Antibodies: Negative; Orbital_CT: No evidence of orbital mass, inflammation, or acute sinus disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal coagulation and negative autoimmune markers, I must consider idiopathic causes or rare vascular anomalies. Do you have a history of recent head trauma, or have you noticed any pulsatile sounds in your ears? REQUEST TEST: MRA_Head_and_Neck

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive vision loss and retinal findings with normal systemic workup, I need to specifically evaluate for optic nerve pathology. Have you noticed any pain with eye movement or central visual field defects, and do you have a history of multiple sclerosis? REQUEST TEST: Visual_Field_Test, OCT_Optic_Nerve

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive vision loss, retinal hemorrhages, and headache in an elderly patient with a negative systemic workup strongly suggests a localized vascular event. DIAGNOSIS READY: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
